documents.title: Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Intimation
Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Bhansali Engineering Polymers Limited reported a 53.3% YoY increase in revenue from operations to ₹ 472.2 crores for Q1 FY27, with PAT rising 42.9% YoY to ₹ 65.6 crores. The company is executing an ongoing capex of approximately ₹ 200 crores to expand its capacity from 75,000 MTPA to 100,000 MTPA, with commissioning targeted by 30 September, 2026. Management expects optimal utilization of this expanded capacity by the end of FY28. The company remains debt-free with a strong balance sheet funded through internal accruals. Bhansali Engineering Polymers Limited reported a revenue of INR 1,276.0 crores for FY26, representing an 8.7% decrease YoY, while EBITDA grew by 1.3% to INR 255.2 crores.

guidance.claim: The company expects optimal utilization of the expanded capacity by the end of FY28.
guidance.quote: Optimal utilisation of expanded capacity expected by end of FY28.

guidance.claim: Commissioning of the enhanced ABS capacity is expected to be completed by the end of September 2026.
guidance.quote: The balance engineering, procurement and construction work is in progress and the commissioning of enhanced capacity is expected to be completed by end of September, 2026.

demand_outlook.claim: Robust growth in consumer durables and automotive industries is expected to drive domestic demand for ABS.
demand_outlook.quote: Robust growth in end-user industries like consumer durables (air conditioners, refrigerators) and automotive will drive the domestic demand for ABS.

demand_outlook.claim: The global market is shifting away from commoditized transparent resins toward specialty and colored grades.
demand_outlook.quote: The global market is shifting toward specialty & colored grades, moving away from commoditized transparent resins to higher-margin applications.

demand_outlook.claim: The IMD's June forecast indicates a normal-to-above-normal monsoon for 2026, which is expected to support rural demand.
demand_outlook.quote: The IMD's June forecast indicates a normal-to-above-normal monsoon for 2026, reducing El Niño risk — a meaningful positive for rural demand and food inflation.

demand_outlook.claim: India's automobile industry achieved record annual sales of approximately 2.83 crore vehicles in FY 2025-26, representing a growth of 10.4%.
demand_outlook.quote: India’s automobile industry recorded its highest-ever annual sales of approximately 2.83 crore vehicles in FY 2025-26, registering growth of 10.4% over the previous year, reflecting strong demand across passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, commercial vehicles and three-wheelers, supported by a series of structural policy reforms that have strengthened demand fundamentals and significantly boosted consumer confidence.

demand_outlook.claim: The long-term outlook for engineering thermoplastics used in household appliances remains positive.
demand_outlook.quote: Accordingly, the long-term outlook for engineering thermoplastics used in household appliances remains positive.

capex_expansion.claim: Implementation of ABS capacity expansion from 75,000 TPA to 1,00,000 TPA is in progress with orders placed for critical long-delivery equipment.
capex_expansion.quote: The implementation of capacity expansion from existing 75000 TPA to 1,00,000 TPA is progressing well and orders have been placed for critical long delivery equipments.

capex_expansion.claim: Engineering, procurement, and construction work is ongoing to complete the commissioning of expanded ABS capacity by end of September 2026.
capex_expansion.quote: The balance engineering, procurement and construction work is in progress and the commissioning of enhanced capacity is expected to be completed by end of September, 2026.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA increased by 44.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹ 92.3 crores, with margins at 19.2%.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA increased by 44.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹ 92.3 crores, from ₹ 63.9 crores in Q1 FY26, with margins at 19.2% for Q1 FY27 as compared to 20.0% in Q1 FY26.

margins_costs.claim: For FY26, EBITDA grew by 1.3% to INR 255.2 crores, with margins at 20.0%.
margins_costs.quote: for FY26, EBITDA grew by 1.3% to INR 255.2 crores, with margins at 20.0%.

margins_costs.claim: The operating margin for FY 2025-26 reached 19.42% compared to 17.43% for FY 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: The operating margin for FY 2025-26 was 19.42 % as compared to 17.43 % for FY 2024-25, whereas the net profit margin stood at 14.14 % as compared to 12.86 % for the previous FY.

margins_costs.claim: Profit before tax margin for FY 2025-26 stood at 19.42% compared to 17.43% for FY 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: The Profit before Tax for FY 2025-26 stood at 19.42 % as compared to 17.43 % for FY 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: The company produced 71,601 TPA against an installed capacity of 75,000 TPA during FY 2025-26.
orders_capacity.quote: During FY 2025-26, the Company achieved production volume of 71601 TPA against installed capacity of 75,000 TPA.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volume for FY 2025-26 stood at 71,501 TPA compared to 74,381 TPA in the prior year.
orders_capacity.quote: Sales volume stood at 71501 TPA (Previous year - 74381 TPA).

capital_allocation.claim: The company maintains a debt-free balance sheet to ensure zero financial risk.
capital_allocation.quote: Debt-free balance sheet ensures zero financial risk and high resilience.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board declared three interim dividends of Re. 1/- each and recommended a final dividend of Re. 1/- per equity share for FY 2025-26.
capital_allocation.quote: Continuing with the practice of rewarding shareholders, the Board declared three Interim Dividends, each of Re.1/- (collectively 300%) per Equity shares of Re.1/- and recommended a Final Dividend of Re.1/- (100 %) per Equity Share for the Financial Year Ended 31st March, 2026.

capital_allocation.claim: The company continues to operate with zero debt.
capital_allocation.quote: The Company continues to enjoy the status of a “Zero Debt Company”.

capital_allocation.claim: The company expects to fund its business operations through internal accruals.
capital_allocation.quote: There was no change in financing pattern and the Company would be able to sustain its business operations through internal accruals.

risks_headwinds.claim: Oil importing nations have faced the main impact of economic shocks resulting from the Iran conflict.
risks_headwinds.quote: Oil importers — India, Japan, South Korea, much of Europe — have borne the brunt of the shock.

risks_headwinds.claim: The domestic ABS business is exposed to foreign exchange risks as main raw materials Styrene and Acrylonitrile are entirely imported.
risks_headwinds.quote: The ABS business in India is exposed to the risk of foreign exchange fluctuations, as the key raw materials viz. ‘Styrene’ and ‘Acrylonitrile’ are import dependent, as there is no indigenous producer for these monomers.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects optimal utilization of the expanded capacity by the end of FY28.
management_commitments.quote: Optimal utilisation of expanded capacity expected by end of FY28.

management_commitments.claim: The commissioning of enhanced capacity from 75,000 TPA to 1,00,000 TPA is expected to be completed by end of September 2026.
management_commitments.quote: The balance engineering, procurement and construction work is in progress and the commissioning of enhanced capacity is expected to be completed by end of September, 2026.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
